question: Among the schools with an SAT excellence rate of over 0.3, what is the highest eligible free rate for students aged 5-17?
evidence: Excellence rate = NumGE1500 / NumTstTakr; Eligible free rates for students aged 5-17 = `Free Meal Count (Ages 5-17)` / `Enrollment (Ages 5-17)`
gold_sql: SELECT MAX(CAST(T1.`Free Meal Count (Ages 5-17)` AS REAL) / T1.`Enrollment (Ages 5-17)`) FROM frpm AS T1 INNER JOIN satscores AS T2 ON T1.CDSCode = T2.cds WHERE CAST(T2.NumGE1500 AS REAL) / T2.NumTstTakr > 0.3
candidate_sqls:
SELECT MAX(CAST(f."Free Meal Count (Ages 5-17)" AS REAL) / f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)") AS highest_free_rate
FROM satscores s
INNER JOIN frpm f ON s.cds = f."CDSCode"
WHERE s.NumGE1500 IS NOT NULL 
AND s.NumTstTakr > 0 
AND s.NumGE1500 IS NOT NULL
AND s.NumTstTakr IS NOT NULL
AND (CAST(s.NumGE1500 AS REAL) / s.NumTstTakr) > 0.3
AND f."Free Meal Count (Ages 5-17)" IS NOT NULL
AND f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)" IS NOT NULL
AND f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)" > 0

SELECT MAX(CAST(f.FREE_MEAL_COUNT__AGES_5_17_ AS REAL) / f.ENROLLMENT__AGES_5_17_) AS highest_eligible_free_rate
FROM satscores s
JOIN frpm f ON s.cds = f.CDSCode
WHERE (CAST(s.NumGE1500 AS REAL) / s.NumTstTakr) > 0.3
AND s.NumTstTakr > 0
AND f.ENROLLMENT__AGES_5_17_ > 0

SELECT MAX(`Free Meal Count (Ages 5-17)` * 1.0 / `Enrollment (Ages 5-17)`)
FROM satscores 
JOIN frpm ON satscores.cds = frpm.CDSCode
WHERE (NumGE1500 * 1.0 / NumTstTakr) > 0.3 
AND NumTstTakr IS NOT NULL AND NumTstTakr > 0
AND `Enrollment (Ages 5-17)` IS NOT NULL AND `Enrollment (Ages 5-17)` > 0
AND `Free Meal Count (Ages 5-17)` IS NOT NULL
